chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn Hammad ibn Zayd from his father from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever gives food to a fasting person will have a reward equal to his, without any decrease, and the reward of the good deeds he performed with the strength of that food."

key_terms.فَطَّرَ: gave food to (specifically to break a fast)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for feeding a fasting person in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, emphasizes the multiplicative reward of *Iftar* (breaking the fast), where the feeder attains a reward equal to the fasting person’s without any deduction. It further introduces the concept of cumulative reward for the specific good deeds performed by the fasters due to the physical strength provided by the meal, highlighting the social and spiritual impact of charitable feeding in Shia jurisprudence.
